name: HALO-WAIT-1-no-wait
note: The bug itself: a crossing into a halo still minting falls through to the ordinary join, which closes my cell and every halo and wipes the roster.

name: HALO-WAIT-2-no-pose-while-waiting
note: The host sends no pose while it calls join, so a wait that sends none stands me still for the others until the halo opens.

name: HALO-WAIT-3-waits-on-an-open-halo-too
note: An open halo is promoted at once; waiting on it instead holds the crossing until HALO_WAIT_MS runs out, and then the ordinary join tears every socket down - the bug back, later.

name: HALO-WAIT-4-waits-with-my-own-cell-down
note: A cell whose socket is down is no place to wait in: the crossing would hold me in a room that hears nothing from me.

name: HALO-WAIT-5-the-wait-never-ends
note: Unbounded, the wait's own bound is gone and only tick's A7 drop (past BACKOFF_MAX_MS, in the same frame's tick) ends it - the bound would then live in another slice's constant and comparison, a frame later.

name: HALO-WAIT-6-the-wait-a-millisecond-short
note: The bound is the halo's own connecting life, to the millisecond; the pin waits to its last.

name: HALO-WAIT-7-the-lists-cleared-before-the-wait
note: The host calls join every frame of the wait: an asked list cleared there is cleared every frame, and a stranger is asked every frame.

name: HALO-WAIT-8-the-hold-before-the-wait
note: A crossing into a halo still connecting waits out the host's 500 ms hold first, and the host sends no pose during it: every such crossing stands me still for half a second.

name: HALO-WAIT-9-no-hold-at-all
note: A crossing with nothing to wait for (a dropped halo) is joined the ordinary way in its first frame: an edge paced at a dropped halo tears every socket down at every step, which the hold exists to prevent (AUDIT ONLINE D11).

name: HALO-WAIT-10-the-host-asks-inRoom
note: The host's own line: asking inRoom alone, a crossing into a halo still connecting waits out the hold with no pose.
